queries.title: 01 · Establish the data scale
queries.sql:
SELECT
  'silver.interactions' AS dataset,
  count(*) AS row_count,
  count(DISTINCT user_id) AS entity_count
FROM silver_interactions
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'silver.items' AS dataset,
  count(*) AS row_count,
  count(DISTINCT parent_asin) AS entity_count
FROM silver_items
ORDER BY dataset
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
How large is the current contract-checked silver data plane?
The counts come from the full local DuckDB silver mirrors, not display constants.

queries.title: 02 · Map the catalog concentration
queries.sql:
SELECT
  coalesce(nullif(trim(main_category), ''), 'Unknown') AS category,
  count(*) AS items,
  round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (), 2) AS catalog_pct
FROM silver_items
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY items DESC, category
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
Which product categories dominate the 1.61M-item catalog?
Concentration is measured over every silver item at the current build state.

queries.title: 03 · Trace cross-category purchase paths
queries.sql:
WITH top_categories AS (
  SELECT coalesce(nullif(trim(main_category), ''), 'Unknown') AS category
  FROM silver_items
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY count(*) DESC
  LIMIT 12
), user_categories AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    i.user_id,
    coalesce(nullif(trim(m.main_category), ''), 'Unknown') AS category
  FROM silver_interactions AS i
  JOIN silver_items AS m USING (parent_asin)
  JOIN top_categories AS t
    ON t.category = coalesce(nullif(trim(m.main_category), ''), 'Unknown')
  WHERE i.verified_purchase IS TRUE
), category_pairs AS (
  SELECT
    a.category AS category_a,
    b.category AS category_b,
    count(*) AS shared_buyers
  FROM user_categories AS a
  JOIN user_categories AS b
    ON a.user_id = b.user_id AND a.category < b.category
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT category_a, category_b, shared_buyers
FROM category_pairs
ORDER BY shared_buyers DESC, category_a, category_b
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
Which leading category pairs share the most verified purchasers?
The query scans the interaction-item join and deduplicates each user-category edge first.

queries.title: 04 · Test the personalization crossover
queries.sql:
SELECT
  model,
  history_depth,
  ndcg10_delta_vs_popularity,
  ci_lo,
  ci_hi,
  excludes_zero
FROM amazon_null_segments
ORDER BY model, history_order
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
Does any personalized Amazon arm beat recent popularity as user history grows?
These paired TEST deltas retain their bootstrap intervals across all five frozen depth buckets.

queries.title: 05 · Find the contrast-regime crossover
queries.sql:
SELECT
  history_depth,
  n_users,
  ndcg10_delta_vs_popularity,
  ci_lo,
  ci_hi,
  q_value,
  bh_significant
FROM ml32m_deep_buckets
ORDER BY history_order
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
Does the null survive in the lower-churn ML-32M contrast regime?
The confirmatory deep buckets show the declared n*=20 NDCG@10 counterexample.

queries.title: 06 · Stress-test the counterexample
queries.sql:
SELECT
  history_depth,
  n_users,
  ndcg10_delta_vs_popularity,
  ci_lo,
  ci_hi,
  q_value,
  bh_significant,
  recall20_metric_robust
FROM ml32m_caveat_buckets
ORDER BY history_order
LIMIT 20
queries.comment:
What prevents the ML-32M crossover from becoming a universal win claim?
Depth-0 users lose sharply and the independent Recall@20 guard does not confirm the winning buckets.
